messages:
Alyssa: heads-up — got flaky streaming hangs in the py SDK when running under our Poetry devenv. Repro is small: async streaming call just stalls after first chunk. Filed a minimal repro and a draft fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1234 :eyes:

Ben: thanks. Does it repro on both httpx 0.23.x and 1.x? We had a split where pinned transitive httpcore caused TLS reuse issues.

Alyssa: i only saw it on the project's lockfile (poetry) which pins httpx==0.23.4 / httpcore==0.15.0. 1.x seems fine locally but CI uses the lockfile so flaky CI runs.

Maria: can you paste the minimal async snippet you used?

Alyssa: sure — here's the repro script (very small):
```py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def stream():
    c = AsyncClient(api_key="REDWOOD_TEST")
    async for chunk in c.chat.stream("hello world"):
        print(chunk)
        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)

asyncio.run(stream())
```

Sam: looks sane. Any traceback when it hangs or just silence?

Alyssa: just silence — process stays alive, no exception, socket open. Curl to hosted endpoint returns chunks fine. Only the SDK streaming iterator stalls.

Ben: that smells like an httpcore connection pooling / keep-alive edge. We had a similar issue fixed by forcing httpx to use async HTTP/1 and disabling http2 in the transport for older httpcore. Can you try overriding the transport in the repro?

Alyssa: tried that: setting `httpx.AsyncClient(http2=False)` in the SDK client wrapper briefly mitigated but didn't fully root-cause. Also saw mismatch between mypy types for the streaming iterator (Iterator[str] vs AsyncIterator[str]) causing CI type failures in the integration test.

Maria: juggling both runtime hang + typing mismatch is annoying. For the typing side, we've standardized on AsyncIterator[str] in the async client helpers — open a tiny typing-only PR if you want, that'll unblock CI.

Alyssa: yep opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1235 for the typing fix. CI on that one passed locally but failed in org CI due to the lockfile pin.

devex-bot: CI (sdk-main): #1234 — tests failing on linux-py39, flake8: no issues, integration: streaming_integration_test.py (hang) — 1 job timed out.

Ben: can you add a debug flag to the client to log the httpcore events? We have an env var HTTPX_DEBUG=1 pattern. If we can capture the state when it stalls we might see a reconnect/keep-alive skip.

Alyssa: adding logging now and will push a log dump to the PR. Also trying a temporary workaround in CI to pin httpcore==0.16 (if that exists) or upgrade httpx to 1.x in the lockfile to see if CI stabilizes.

Sam: FYI when you change the lockfile in a PR, add a small changelog note and ping infra to rebuild the cache image. We had cached wheels that made CI inconsistent between branches.

Maria: for the release/train: if the root cause is httpcore, we should add a compatibility note to the SDK docs and a recommended lockfile fragment to paste into pyproject. That reduces support churn.

Alyssa: sounds good. Plan: (1) push debug logs to #1234, (2) open small typing PR #1235, (3) try lockfile bump in a branch and run CI, (4) if repro confirmed, add docs snippet + patch. Pinging @Ben for review on the transport/logging change.

Ben: will review later today. If urgent, leave a review request and i'll prioritize.

Alyssa: thanks — will request review after I push the logs. :thumbsup:

devex-bot: CI (sdk-main): #1235 — typing-only PR — all checks passed (mypy, unit).

Maria: awesome — merge the typing PR first, that'll at least make the other PRs cleaner in history.

Alyssa: merged #1235. Next I'll try a lockfile bump branch and post results here.

Sam: thanks for doing the coordination. small ask — add a short note in the PR description about which Poetry / pipx / pip combinations were tested so QE can reproduce.

Alyssa: will do.

Ben: once we have deterministic repro logs, we can decide if we need to vendor a tiny shim or just document the required pins.
